claim: Inflammation in ulcerative colitis is typically restricted to the mucosal layer of distal gut.
source: Inflammation in ulcerative colitis is typically restricted to the mucosal layer of distal gut.
evidence: This is a general statement about UC pathology presented in the abstract without specific experimental data or citations in this sentence.

claim: Disrupted mucus barrier, coupled with microbial dysbiosis, has been reported to occur prior to the onset of inflammation.
source: Disrupted mucus barrier, coupled with microbial dysbiosis, has been reported to occur prior to the onset of inflammation.
evidence: This statement references prior reports but does not include specific citations in this sentence of the abstract.

claim: Rab7 expression is lowered in goblet cells of colon during human and murine colitis.
source: We identified a lowered Rab7 expression in goblet cells of colon during human and murine colitis.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in the manuscript.

claim: In vivo Rab7 knocked down mice displayed a compromised mucus layer.
source: In vivo Rab7 knocked down mice (Rab7KD) displayed a compromised mucus layer, increased microbial permeability, and depleted gut microbiota with enhanced susceptibility to dextran sodium-sulfate induced colitis.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data in the manuscript.

claim: In vivo Rab7 knocked down mice displayed increased microbial permeability.
source: In vivo Rab7 knocked down mice (Rab7KD) displayed a compromised mucus layer, increased microbial permeability, and depleted gut microbiota with enhanced susceptibility to dextran sodium-sulfate induced colitis.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data in the manuscript.

claim: In vivo Rab7 knocked down mice displayed depleted gut microbiota.
source: In vivo Rab7 knocked down mice (Rab7KD) displayed a compromised mucus layer, increased microbial permeability, and depleted gut microbiota with enhanced susceptibility to dextran sodium-sulfate induced colitis.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data in the manuscript.

claim: In vivo Rab7 knocked down mice displayed enhanced susceptibility to dextran sodium-sulfate induced colitis.
source: In vivo Rab7 knocked down mice (Rab7KD) displayed a compromised mucus layer, increased microbial permeability, and depleted gut microbiota with enhanced susceptibility to dextran sodium-sulfate induced colitis.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data in the manuscript.

claim: Abnormalities in Rab7KD mice emerged owing to altered mucus composition.
source: These abnormalities emerged owing to altered mucus composition, as revealed by mucus proteomics, with increased expression of mucin protease chloride channel accessory 1 (CLCA1).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data including mucus proteomics analysis.

claim: Mucus proteomics revealed increased expression of CLCA1 in Rab7KD mice.
source: These abnormalities emerged owing to altered mucus composition, as revealed by mucus proteomics, with increased expression of mucin protease chloride channel accessory 1 (CLCA1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from mass spectrometry analysis of mucus samples.

claim: Rab7 maintained optimal CLCA1 levels by controlling its lysosomal degradation.
source: Mechanistically, Rab7 maintained optimal CLCA1 levels by controlling its lysosomal degradation, a process that was dysregulated during colitis.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding supported by experimental data including bafilomycin treatment and colocalization studies.

claim: The process of Rab7-mediated CLCA1 lysosomal degradation was dysregulated during colitis.
source: Mechanistically, Rab7 maintained optimal CLCA1 levels by controlling its lysosomal degradation, a process that was dysregulated during colitis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations in colitis models.

claim: Intestinal epithelium and local immune cells execute diverse regulatory mechanisms to maintain intestinal homeostasis.
source: On a cellular level, intestinal epithelium and local immune cells execute diverse regulatory mechanisms to maintain this intestinal homeostasis (Maloy and Powrie, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Goblet cells participate in intestinal homeostasis by secreting mucins that form mucus layer.
source: Goblet cells, a specialized epithelial cell type, participate by secreting mucins that form mucus layer, functioning as the first line of defense against the microbial population (Johansson and Hansson, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Mucus layer functions as the first line of defense against the microbial population.
source: Goblet cells, a specialized epithelial cell type, participate by secreting mucins that form mucus layer, functioning as the first line of defense against the microbial population (Johansson and Hansson, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Impairment in mucus layer has been observed before intestinal inflammation in ulcerative colitis.
source: Impairment in mucus layer has been observed before intestinal inflammation in ulcerative colitis (UC), one of the two major forms of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) (Boltin et al., 2013; Johansson et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Active UC patients exhibit reduced number of goblet cells.
source: Active UC patients exhibit reduced number of goblet cells and a compromised mucus layer (Singh et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Active UC patients exhibit a compromised mucus layer.
source: Active UC patients exhibit reduced number of goblet cells and a compromised mucus layer (Singh et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Two stratified layers of mucus exist in colon: a loose outer layer permeable to the luminal flora and a dense adherent sterile inner layer.
source: Two stratified layers of mucus exist in colon: a loose outer layer permeable to the luminal flora and a dense adherent sterile inner layer (Atuma et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The core structure of mucus is formed of Muc2.
source: The core structure of mucus is formed of Muc2.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mucus composition.

claim: FCGBP, CLCA1, TFF3, and ZG16 are known protein constituents of mucus layer.
source: Several other known protein constituents of mucus layer are FCGBP, CLCA1, TFF3, and ZG16 (Hansson and Johansson, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CLCA1 is a metalloprotease exclusively secreted by goblet cells.
source: Chloride channel accessory 1 (CLCA1) is a metalloprotease exclusively secreted by goblet cells and forms one of the major non-mucin components of mucus (Nyström et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CLCA1 forms one of the major non-mucin components of mucus.
source: Chloride channel accessory 1 (CLCA1) is a metalloprotease exclusively secreted by goblet cells and forms one of the major non-mucin components of mucus (Nyström et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CLCA1 has Muc2 cleaving properties.
source: It has Muc2 cleaving properties and thus is involved in intestinal mucus dynamics and homeostasis (Nyström et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CLCA1 is involved in intestinal mucus dynamics and homeostasis.
source: It has Muc2 cleaving properties and thus is involved in intestinal mucus dynamics and homeostasis (Nyström et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: SENP7 plays a critical role in IBD pathophysiology.
source: In a recent report focusing on epithelial-immunocyte crosstalk, our group demonstrated a critical role of SENP7, a deSUMOylase in IBD pathophysiology (Suhail et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors' group.

claim: Rab7 was observed to physically interact with SENP7 in murine model of IBD.
source: Interestingly, Rab7, among the several other Rab GTPases identified to physically interact with SENP7, was observed in murine model of IBD.
evidence: This is an observation from prior work that motivated the current study.

claim: Rab7 protein participates in vesicular transport of a cell.
source: Rab7 protein participates in vesicular transport of a cell, influencing protein turnover, secretion, autophagy, and intracellular pathogen survival (Deffieu et al., 2021; Gutierrez et al., 2004; Mohapatra et al., 2018; Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Yap et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Rab7 influences protein turnover.
source: Rab7 protein participates in vesicular transport of a cell, influencing protein turnover, secretion, autophagy, and intracellular pathogen survival (Deffieu et al., 2021; Gutierrez et al., 2004; Mohapatra et al., 2018; Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Yap et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Rab7 influences secretion.
source: Rab7 protein participates in vesicular transport of a cell, influencing protein turnover, secretion, autophagy, and intracellular pathogen survival (Deffieu et al., 2021; Gutierrez et al., 2004; Mohapatra et al., 2018; Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Yap et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Rab7 influences autophagy.
source: Rab7 protein participates in vesicular transport of a cell, influencing protein turnover, secretion, autophagy, and intracellular pathogen survival (Deffieu et al., 2021; Gutierrez et al., 2004; Mohapatra et al., 2018; Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Yap et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Rab7 influences intracellular pathogen survival.
source: Rab7 protein participates in vesicular transport of a cell, influencing protein turnover, secretion, autophagy, and intracellular pathogen survival (Deffieu et al., 2021; Gutierrez et al., 2004; Mohapatra et al., 2018; Vanlandingham and Ceresa, 2009; Yap et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Rab7 protein expression is significantly reduced in whole colon tissue of DSS-treated mice compared to healthy control.
source: A significant reduction in Rab7 protein was seen in tissue lysates of distal colon from DSS mice compared to healthy control (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Rab7 protein is ubiquitously present over whole colon tissue with intensified expression in crypts and epithelium in healthy mice.
source: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) of colon sections revealed the ubiquitous presence of Rab7 protein over whole tissue with intensified expression in crypts and other zones of epithelium in healthy mice which got significantly lessened in DSS mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, inset).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by IHC data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Rab7 expression in crypts and epithelium is significantly lessened in DSS mice.
source: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) of colon sections revealed the ubiquitous presence of Rab7 protein over whole tissue with intensified expression in crypts and other zones of epithelium in healthy mice which got significantly lessened in DSS mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, inset).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by IHC data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Increased duration of DSS treatment resulted in a gradual decrease in mice body weight.
source: Increased duration of DSS treatment resulted in a gradual decrease in mice body weight (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and colon length (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) in DSS 7 and DSS 5 mice when compared with DSS 3 mice.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Increased duration of DSS treatment resulted in decreased colon length in DSS 7 and DSS 5 mice when compared with DSS 3 mice.
source: Increased duration of DSS treatment resulted in a gradual decrease in mice body weight (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and colon length (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) in DSS 7 and DSS 5 mice when compared with DSS 3 mice.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: DSS 5 and DSS 7 mice displayed increased splenomegaly.
source: DSS 5 and DSS 7 mice also displayed increased splenomegaly (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E) ,mirroring severe inflammation seen during human IBD.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Whole colonic tissue lysate and crypts showed upregulated expression of Rab7 at the early inflammation states (DSS 3–5).
source: While whole colonic tissue lysate and crypts (isolated from colons of mice) showed upregulated expression of Rab7 at the early inflammation states (DSS 3–5) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F), interestingly, the intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) displayed significant reduction in expression of Rab7 at this stage (day 3) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Intestinal epithelial cells displayed significant reduction in expression of Rab7 at day 3 of DSS treatment.
source: While whole colonic tissue lysate and crypts (isolated from colons of mice) showed upregulated expression of Rab7 at the early inflammation states (DSS 3–5) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F), interestingly, the intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) displayed significant reduction in expression of Rab7 at this stage (day 3) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Rab7 gene expression is downregulated approximately 11-fold in UC patient colonic biopsies relative to healthy controls.
source: qRT-PCR of 22 colonoscopy tissue samples each of UC and controls revealed ~–11-fold downregulation of Rab7 in colitis relative to healthy controls (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Rab7 downregulation in UC patients is evident at protein levels.
source: The downregulation was also evident at protein levels as revealed by immunoblotting (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Similar pattern of Rab7 downregulation is visible in Crohn's disease.
source: In Crohn's disease (CD), another form of IBD, similar pattern was visible (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G and H.

claim: A decrease in Rab7 expression was observed in mild UC patients at the transcriptional level.
source: At the transcriptional level, a decrease in Rab7 expression was observed in mild UC patients, with even more reduction in moderate patients compared to controls (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Even more reduction in Rab7 expression was observed in moderate UC patients compared to controls at the transcriptional level.
source: At the transcriptional level, a decrease in Rab7 expression was observed in mild UC patients, with even more reduction in moderate patients compared to controls (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The lowering of Rab7 expression was correlative to disease severity.
source: The lowering of expression was correlative to disease severity as noticed by immunoblotting and immunohistochemistry (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: Similar expression alteration of Rab7 was observed in UC remission patients.
source: Notably, similar expression alteration of Rab7 was observed in UC remission patients (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Variations in Rab7 expression levels can be attributed to the extent of gut inflammation.
source: Taken together, our data suggests that variations in Rab7 expression levels can be attributed to the extent of gut inflammation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing Rab7 expression at different stages of inflammation.

claim: Rab7 is expressed in cells having a vacuolated morphology, a specific characteristic of goblet cells of the epithelium.
source: A closer look revealed that the staining was higher in cells having a vacuolated morphology, a specific characteristic of goblet cells of the epithelium (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by IHC data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Colocalizing Rab7 with UEA1 confirmed dominant expression in goblet cells of intestine.
source: Further, colocalizing Rab7 with UEA1, a goblet cell-specific marker, confirmed dominant expression in secretory cells of intestine, that is, goblet cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Rab7 was seen in both crypt base and inter crypt goblet cells.
source: Notably, Rab7 was seen in both crypt base and inter crypt goblet cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, inset).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Rab7 levels are significantly reduced distinctively in goblet cells of DSS mice compared to control mice.
source: Interestingly, immunofluorescence-based staining of Rab7 and goblet cells in colonic sections of DSS mice revealed significantly reduced levels of Rab7 distinctively in goblet cells compared to control mice (Figure 2A and BFigure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Similar results of reduced Rab7 in goblet cells were obtained in UC patient colonic biopsy sections with respect to healthy controls.
source: Similar results were obtained in the case of UC patient colonic biopsy sections with respect to healthy controls (Figure 2C and DFigure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Differentiated HT29 goblet-like cells showed an increased expression of Rab7 compared to undifferentiated HT29 cells.
source: Interestingly, compared to undifferentiated HT29 cells, these goblet-like cells showed an increased expression of Rab7 (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by immunofluorescence and western blot data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Rab7 protein is present in the vicinity of secretory vesicles in HT29-MTX-E12 cells.
source: Moreover, ultrastructural details (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G) showed Rab7 protein to be present in the vicinity of secretory vesicles (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by immune-EM data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Rab7 may be involved in regulating the goblet cell function in the intestine.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that Rab7 may be involved in regulating the goblet cell function in the intestine.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing Rab7 localization and expression in goblet cells.

claim: Only 4 days of DSS administration was sufficient to generate severe inflammation in Rab7KD mice.
source: Interestingly, only 4 d of DSS administration was sufficient to generate severe inflammation in Rab7KD mice which was atypical for DSS-colitis model.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the Rab7 knockdown mouse model.

claim: Severe inflammation in Rab7KD mice after 4 days of DSS was atypical for DSS-colitis model.
source: Interestingly, only 4 d of DSS administration was sufficient to generate severe inflammation in Rab7KD mice which was atypical for DSS-colitis model.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the Rab7 knockdown mouse model.

claim: Severe inflammation in Rab7KD mice was evident by reduced body weight.
source: This was evident by reduced body weight (Figure 3B), diarrhea, and rectal bleeding (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Severe inflammation in Rab7KD mice was evident by diarrhea.
source: This was evident by reduced body weight (Figure 3B), diarrhea, and rectal bleeding (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Severe inflammation in Rab7KD mice was evident by rectal bleeding.
source: This was evident by reduced body weight (Figure 3B), diarrhea, and rectal bleeding (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Almost 50% of Rab7 protein expression was reduced in Rab7KD mice groups.
source: Almost 50% of protein expression was reduced in Rab7KD mice groups, thus confirming successful knockdown (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: No significant alterations in Rab7 expression were visible in spleen, MLN, and liver, proving no off-targeting of nucleic acid by nanogel.
source: No significant alterations in Rab7 expression were visible in other organs such as spleen, MLN, and liver, proving no off-targeting of nucleic acid by nanogel (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: DSS and DSS+CScr mice showed a significant reduction in colon length with inflamed appearance compared to the C, CScr, and Rab7KD groups.
source: DSS and DSS+CScr mice showed a significant reduction in colon length with inflamed appearance compared to the C, CScr, and Rab7KD groups (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The features of inflammation were more severe in the DSS+Rab7KD group compared to DSS+CScr mice.
source: Notably, the features were more severe in the case of DSS+Rab7KD group compared to DSS+CScr mice.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the Rab7 knockdown mouse model.

claim: Splenomegaly was observed in DSS+Rab7KD group depicting higher inflammation.
source: In line with this, we observed splenomegaly in DSS+Rab7KD group depicting higher inflammation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: H&E staining of distal colon of DSS+Rab7KD mice showed exacerbated signs of inflammation such as immune cell infiltration, colonic wall thickening, goblet cell and crypt loss, and epithelial erosion.
source: H&E staining of distal colon of DSS+ Rab7KD mice showed exacerbated signs of inflammation such as immune cell infiltration, colonic wall thickening, goblet cell and crypt loss, and epithelial erosion (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by histology data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The intensity of inflammation signs was higher in DSS+Rab7KD group as can be seen in the histopathology score plot.
source: While many of these signs were evident in DSS+CScr mice, in the DSS+Rab7KD group the intensity was higher as can be seen in the histopathology score plot (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by histopathology scoring data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: ELISA revealed a significant upregulation of TNFα in DSS+CScr mice.
source: ELISA revealed a significant upregulation of TNFα in DSS+CScr mice, which was further higher in DSS+Rab7KD mice (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: TNFα was further higher in DSS+Rab7KD mice compared to DSS+CScr mice.
source: ELISA revealed a significant upregulation of TNFα in DSS+CScr mice, which was further higher in DSS+Rab7KD mice (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Downregulation of Rab7 heightens DSS-induced colitis in mice.
source: These data led us to conclude that downregulation of Rab7 heightens DSS-induced colitis in mice, thus hinting toward its functional importance during colitis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in the Rab7 knockdown mouse model.

claim: DSS-treated mice groups showed a significantly decreased Alcian blue staining, indicating reduced goblet cell number.
source: DSS-treated mice groups showed a significantly decreased staining, indicating reduced goblet cell number.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by Alcian blue staining data.

claim: The decrease in goblet cell number was accompanied by thinning of the mucus layer in both the DSS-treated mice groups.
source: As expected, the decrease in goblet cell number was accompanied by thinning of the mucus layer in both the DSS-treated mice groups (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In Rab7KD mice IML was significantly much wider and seemed to be less dense showing a lighter stain of Alcian blue.
source: Surprisingly, in Rab7KD mice IML was significantly much wider and seemed to be less dense showing a lighter stain of Alcian blue (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Muc2 protein was seen to be not forming a theca and was scattered over cell cytoplasm in HEK RAB7-/- cells compared to wildtype cells.
source: Surprisingly, the Muc2 protein was seen to be not forming a theca and was scattered over cell cytoplasm compared to wildtype cells corroborating the above in vivo data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: In control mice, bacteria were detected in the outer mucus layer but not in inner layer.
source: In control mice as anticipated, bacteria were detected in the outer mucus layer but not in inner layer (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by FISH data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In Rab7KD mice, in spite of the mucus layer being wider several bacteria were detected in the inner mucus layer verifying increased permeability.
source: On the contrary, in Rab7KD mice, in spite of the mucus layer being wider several bacteria were detected in the inner mucus layer verifying increased permeability (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by FISH data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: DSS+CScr mice showed a dramatic increase in the number of bacteria penetrating the inner layer.
source: DSS+CScr mice showed a dramatic increase in the number of bacteria penetrating the inner layer.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from FISH analysis.

claim: Rab7 is involved in modulating the mucus-secreting function of goblet cells which further alters the mucus layer characteristics leading to bacterial breach and generation of inflammation.
source: These data clearly indicated toward the involvement of Rab7 in modulating the mucus-secreting function of goblet cells which further alters the mucus layer characteristics leading to bacterial breach and generation of inflammation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on mucus layer and bacterial permeability.

claim: Shannon index plot showed decreased microbial diversity richness and evenness in the DSS+CScr mice groups.
source: As anticipated, Shannon index plot showed decreased microbial diversity richness and evenness in the DSS+CScr mice groups (µmedian = 3.67).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by 16S metagenomic data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The phenotype of decreased microbial diversity was more severe in Rab7KD mice (µmedian = 3.46).
source: This phenotype was more severe in Rab7KD mice (µmedian = 3.46) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by 16S metagenomic data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Principal coordinates analysis indicated that each of the three groups (CScr, Rab7KD, DSS+CScr) assumed a discrete cluster.
source: Further, principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) indicated that each of the three groups assumed a discrete cluster (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by PCoA data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Beta diversity index heatmap revealed differences in the microbial diversity among different experimental mice groups.
source: Beta diversity index heatmap revealed differences in the microbial diversity among different experimental mice groups (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The beta diversity map indicated a shift in microbial diversity in Rab7KD mice such that they appeared to occupy an intermediate position between CScr and DSS+CScr mice.
source: The map clearly indicated a shift in microbial diversity in Rab7KD mice such that they appeared to occupy an intermediate position between CScr and DSS+CScr mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the beta diversity heatmap data.

claim: At the phylum level, bacteroidetes showed an increase in abundance in the Rab7KD and DSS+CScr mice groups.
source: At the phylum level, bacteroidetes showed an increase in abundance, whereas firmicutes were significantly less represented in the Rab7KD and DSS+CScr mice groups (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by 16S metagenomic data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: At the phylum level, firmicutes were significantly less represented in the Rab7KD and DSS+CScr mice groups.
source: At the phylum level, bacteroidetes showed an increase in abundance, whereas firmicutes were significantly less represented in the Rab7KD and DSS+CScr mice groups (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by 16S metagenomic data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Firmicutes are known to get less abundant in IBD.
source: Firmicutes are known to get less abundant in IBD (Frank et al., 2007, Manichanh et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Class level analysis revealed that the firmicutes reduced were clostridia.
source: Class level analysis revealed that the firmicutes reduced were clostridia, while the abundance of Bacteroidia was more among Bacteroidetes (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by 16S metagenomic data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The abundance of Bacteroidia was more among Bacteroidetes.
source: Class level analysis revealed that the firmicutes reduced were clostridia, while the abundance of Bacteroidia was more among Bacteroidetes (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by 16S metagenomic data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Genus such as Lactobacillus and Parabacteroidetes were found to be significantly altered in Rab7KD mice compared to CScr.
source: Genus such as Lactobacillus and Parabacteroidetes were found to be significantly altered in Rab7KD mice compared to CScr (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by 16S metagenomic data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Compared to CScr mice, Rab7KD and DSS+CScr mice showed a decrease in the abundance of a particular category of bacterial species containing probiotic microorganisms.
source: Intriguingly, compared to CScr mice, Rab7KD and DSS+CScr mice showed a decrease in the abundance of a particular category of bacterial species (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, red box). The majority of these contained probiotic microorganisms.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by 16S metagenomic data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Bifidobacterium longum and Lactobacillus helveticus have been thoroughly researched in relation to colitis.
source: These include Bifidobacterium longum and Lactobacillus helveticus, both of which have been thoroughly researched in relation to colitis (Ho et al., 2022; Tamaki et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: No significant change was observed in the total mucin content between any of the groups.
source: No significant change was observed in the total mucin content between any of the groups (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by mucin gel data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: A total of 522 proteins were detected among different mice groups by mass spectrometry.
source: A total of 522 proteins were detected among different mice groups (Figure 6D), of which 288 were common in all along with some unique proteins in each group as is evident through the Venn diagram (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: 288 proteins were common in all groups with some unique proteins in each group.
source: A total of 522 proteins were detected among different mice groups (Figure 6D), of which 288 were common in all along with some unique proteins in each group as is evident through the Venn diagram (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Label-free quantification identified approximately 500 differentially expressed proteins among the samples.
source: Label-free quantification identified approximately 500 differentially expressed proteins among the samples (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Differentially expressed proteins were part of certain pathways over-represented in Gene Ontology analysis like extracellular exosome biogenesis, vesicle localization, and calcium-dependent phospholipase A2 activity.
source: These proteins were part of certain pathways over-represented in Gene Ontology (GO) analysis like extracellular exosome biogenesis, vesicle localization, and calcium-dependent phospholipase A2 activity based on biological processes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B) and molecular function (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by GO analysis data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Certain secretory proteins such as CLCA1, APOA1, and transferrin were seen to be upregulated in the Rab7KD mice group when compared with the CScr.
source: Certain secretory proteins such as chloride channel accessory 1 (CLCA1), apolipoprotein AI (APOA1), and transferrin (Tf) caught our interest as they were seen to be upregulated in the Rab7KD mice group when compared with the CScr (highlighted in red in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: Increased amount of transferrin in mucus indirectly hinted towards the decrease in transferrin receptors (TFRC) in the intestinal cells which uptake them.
